analysis.investment_thesis: Excelsoft is a small Indian EdTech SaaS with genuine switching costs in assessment/proctoring, decent margins, and an almost debt-free balance sheet, but ROE of 10.4% falls short of my 15% hurdle and earnings history is too volatile to trust. At 13x forward P/E and 5.98x EV/EBITDA the price is undemanding, yet the quality simply isn't there to excite me.
key_strengths: Aggressive debt repayment: borrowings slashed from INR 168 Cr (2020) to INR 45 Cr (2025), D/E now just 0.12
Revenue growing at 17.7% 5Y CAGR with operating CF positive all 5 years (INR 53 Cr in FY25)
Global EdTech niche (assessment, proctoring, LMS) creates meaningful switching costs in multi-year institutional contracts
key_risks: ROE only 10.4% — well below my 15% minimum, suggesting the business doesn't earn exceptional returns on capital
Volatile net profit (-5 → 11 → 15 → 22 → 13 → 35 Cr) — no predictability; FY24 profit collapsed 41% before rebounding
FY25 FCF of INR 290 Cr vs OCF of only INR 53 Cr signals a large one-time asset disposal, not genuine cash generation
red_flags: Reserves actually declined (INR 296 Cr → INR 288 Cr) while equity rose INR 91 Cr — implies share issuance diluted existing holders
Other Income surged from INR 2 Cr to INR 15 Cr in FY25, inflating reported net profit of INR 35 Cr; core earnings quality is lower than headline
EBITDA in a contracting 5Y trend despite double-digit revenue growth — operating leverage is running in reverse
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Excelsoft is a niche EdTech SaaS out of Mysore serving universities, schools, and enterprises globally with assessment, proctoring, and LMS products. The switching-cost story is real — once an institution embeds its exam infrastructure into SARAS or EasyProctor, migration is painful. Promoter holding at 59% signals alignment, and the steady debt paydown (INR 123 Cr net reduction over five years) reflects disciplined capital stewardship. At 5.98x EV/EBITDA and 13x forward P/E, the market is pricing this as a sleepy small-cap with limited upside — and I largely agree with that assessment.

What keeps me from getting excited is threefold. First, a 10.4% ROE tells me the business is not truly exceptional; wonderful businesses earn 20-30% ROE sustainably. Second, the FY25 numbers are flattered — INR 15 Cr of other income (up 7x) and a mysterious FCF of INR 290 Cr against OCF of only INR 53 Cr suggest asset sales are doing the heavy lifting. Strip those out and underlying earnings are closer to INR 20-25 Cr, putting the true P/E nearer 35x. Third, the EBITDA trend is contracting even as revenues grow — margins are being squeezed, not expanded. For a ~INR 812 Cr market-cap SaaS company with limited institutional sponsorship (FII + DII barely 5.4%), I'd want far higher quality before committing capital.
